mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month preceding the prediction is associated with a short-term decline in equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative despite FEDFUNDS > 4% for ≥3 consecutive months prior.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in employment (PAYEMS) of at least 2% accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises ≥2% AND UNRATE < 5% in the same month
failure_condition: Significant negative 20-day forward return despite both indicators meeting the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) of 3% for two consecutive months signals accelerating economic demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) during the observed INDPRO expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for three consecutive months suggests supply-side easing, which precedes positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 2.0% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative despite sustained CPIAUCSL < 2%.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly ratio of RSAFS to GDP (implied liquidity) exceeds 1.5 for two consecutive months, it indicates excess liquidity, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS / GDPC1 > 1.5 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in all subsequent 5-day windows with RSAFS/GDPC1 > 1.5.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) to below 4% coinciding with a monthly pay growth (PAYEMS) increase of at least 1% predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0% AND PAYEMS rises ≥1% in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative despite both triggers being met.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) of 10% or more signals a cooling in the housing market, which precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative during periods of HOUST declines ≥10%.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 1% for three consecutive months in a non-recessionary macro context, it predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to lower policy rate uncertainty.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1.0% for three consecutive months and macro context is stable (e.g., GDP growth > 2%)
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive despite the low-rate condition.
